[b]Al-Qadi Orders[/b]
[i]Supreme Leader Falah sits in a dark, underground bunker, situated somewhere on the outskirts of Aduab. He is accompanied by various high command generals.[/i]

The movements throughout New Westmore have been very effective sir, says a senior general, as Falah nods in approval.
Indeed, we seemed to have appealed to the interests of the greater Brunswick shaman community. Im sure we could recruit some of them you know, adds another. Falah finally decides to speak for the first time since the beginning of the meeting.
Really? Well why dont we get on it then! Order the Al-Qadi to begin recruitment tactics,
Yes sir,
Multiple people scurry out of the room, eager to satisfy Falahs demands.

Later that day, a meeting is held with various generals who have been allocated to run the Al-Qadi. In this meeting, the Al-Qadi are ordered to begin immediately recruiting the westmorean shamans of greater Brunswick. They are also told that operations in the ULR need to begin soon, or the supreme leader will take action

[b]Pilot:[/b] Jaabir al-Shaer of Naqazar
[b]Aircraft:[/b] Rasheed-pattern Transport Flyer

The reclusive rat people of the Bakagzi Desert on Shahmat make a surprise appearance in Sikirsk's airshow. Their showcase is relatively short and sweet, though they are showing off an invention important to their own culture and nation. Using a flying machine that resembles a small fishing boat but in the air, the Kwelahn of the Bakagzi Desert can sometimes operate independently of their home Tavariath for weeks at a time, mostly for the purposes of finding food, water sources, and other important resources for the migrating city. Though not capable of complicated aerial acrobatics or airshows like many other, more modern aircraft, the Rasheed-pattern's incredible durability and ability to supply travelers for weeks at a time without stopping is impressive to say the least, indicative of the Kwelahn's engineering prowess and the engineering doctrine influenced by their incredibly unique semi-nomadic way of life.

[i]Only a few individuals are endowed with ancestral power, the Ngankaris, elders endowed with wisdom and responsible for passing on ancient traditions and stories to new generations, are one of them, through sacred rituals such as dances, in places seen as "special" for channeling the Dreamtime, in this case, oases, soakages, or trees, are where the ancestral energy is strongest, and therefore can be used, however, these are healing powers, and only the wisest men develop this technique throughout their lives, being able to cure diseases through "breeze of life" rituals, where the ngankaris controls a light breeze and makes a patient inhale it, curing them of the illnesses that torment them in their lives.
 Elemental magic:
However, it is not only the Ngankaris who are endowed with ancestral power, everyone has some power, but it waits to be awakened, but this only occurs in ritual situations, or through sacred objects, such as Churingas.
Note that such powers cease to exist when the clan's totem ceases to exist, since it is the presence of the ancestral power of that clan.
Perhaps of the clans, the members of the Gadoorbuya clan are the most powerful, since they are direct creations made in the image of the Wonambi (rainbow serpent), they have the gift of controlling water and wind, being able to create gales or know the exact location of underground water and manipulate it to rise, but perhaps among their most unique abilities is the Wanamali, or rainbow orb, made by the most powerful users of the clan, such as Balunji, the leader of the Gadoorbuya clan.
From the Marrapinti Clan, rivals of the Gadoorbuya, they are related to their kangaroo totem, their element is earth, their members are able to control the earth, creating barriers of rocks, or molding them as they wish or raising clouds of sand or earth as they wish, their unique abilities include leaping over humans, which allows them to jump at high altitudes like kangaroos. Their most powerful ability is the Akwalya murrangkua, where the user is able to, with their hands and forcing themselves, shake and crack the ground in nearby areas (not causing an entire earthquake, but a strong tremor and cracks in the ground, in a radius of
The members of the Gunyor clan are known for being gifted with high speed, and control over the winds, they can make a simple breeze turn into a terrible gale, their members are agile and fast, their mastery over the winds allows them to take the air from the lungs of their victims without problems, in addition to being able to make powerful gusts of wind in attacks.
The Betcherry clan, whose totem is the Alkiragunyan parakeet, is perhaps one of the weakest of the clans, but if in good hands, they can be useful.
Its members are capable of manipulating winds lightly, being able to make powerful gusts of wind, but not as powerful as the Gunyor. Their main ability is the Parrunga, a loud cry that confuses enemies and creates false illusions.
The Ngintarra clan, whose totem is the lizard, their members show excellent agility and climbing skills. Their main ability includes the Warlutja, where the individual has their body covered in reptilian scales, making them more resistant and easier to camouflage. The echidna clan, Nynghna, although small in comparison to others, has curious abilities, its members are known for being able to conjure spikes in their skin, and any injury or damage they take is reflected on the aggressor, but it is not just defenses, they can conjure spikes of any size and shape for attack.
Their unique ability is precisely to fill their bodies with spikes that protect them from any aggressor.
Note that each skill has a cost, the Ngankaris give part of their own vitality to heal, and the elementals will lose sanity if they use too many skills, however, it can be replenished if they take a Tjurrupa, a unique word, which refers to something like "a state of relaxation and rest in which you want to empty your mind after intense activities"[/i]
